PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Centre

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Maternal age: 25 years
Gestation: 20 weeks by ultrasound dating
Indication: Screening for chromosomal trisomies

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence-Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Uncultured amniocytes

METHODOLOGY
DNA extracted from uncultured amniocytes. QF-PCR analysis performed using fluorescently labelled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. A minimum of 4 informative markers analysed per chromosome.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13 markers:
D13S631: 1:1 ratio
D13S258: 1:1 ratio
D13S742: 1:1 ratio
D13S628: 1:1 ratio

Chromosome 18 markers:
D18S391: 1:1 ratio
D18S390: 1:1 ratio
D18S535: 1:1 ratio
D18S386: 1:1 ratio

Chromosome 21 markers:
D21S1435: 1:1 ratio
D21S1411: 1:1 ratio
D21S1412: 1:1 ratio
D21S1446: 1:1 ratio

Sex chromosome markers:
AMEL: XX
TAF9: Normal female pattern

CONCLUSION
Normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No abnormality detected.

No evidence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), or trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) in this fetal sample.

RECOMMENDATION
QF-PCR provides rapid screening for common aneuploidies but does not detect all chromosomal abnormalities. Complete full karyotype analysis from cultured amniocytes is recommended to exclude other chromosomal abnormalities including balanced rearrangements, mosaicism, and abnormalities of other chromosomes.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorised by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
